unresolved.reason: The current MFA schedule limits Uruguay to diplomatic or official passports, while current ISS and Trinidad mission schedules expressly state a 90-day ordinary-passport waiver. The Immigration (Passports) Order's default cannot break the tie because it preserves ministerial exemptions and visa-abolition agreements; no current controlling instrument or Uruguayan passport-authority result establishes ordinary scope.

The current MFA schedule limits Indonesia to diplomatic, official or service passports, while current ISS and Trinidad mission schedules list Indonesia for 30 days without that limitation. The Immigration (Passports) Order retains ministerial-exemption and agreement-in-force exceptions, and no current controlling instrument or Indonesian passport-authority result resolves ordinary-passport scope.

The current MFA and Trinidad mission schedules limit Cuba to diplomatic, official or service passports, while the current ISS schedule lists Cuba without a passport-type limitation. The Immigration (Passports) Order's default expressly preserves ministerial exemptions and visa-abolition agreements; no current controlling instrument or Cuban passport-authority result establishes the ordinary-passport rule.
